articles.title: Sam Altman: The Visionary Driving the Artificial Intelligence Revolution
articles.summary: As artificial intelligence transforms industries across the globe, Sam Altman has emerged as one of the most influential technology leaders of the modern era.
articles.content:
As the Chief Executive Officer of OpenAI, Altman has played a central role in advancing generative AI, bringing powerful AI tools to businesses, researchers, and millions of everyday users worldwide.

Early Career


Born on April 22, 1985, in Chicago, Illinois, Sam Altman developed an interest in computers and programming from an early age. He attended Stanford University, where he studied computer science before leaving to pursue entrepreneurship.

His first startup, Loopt, was a location-based social networking company that participated in the prestigious Y Combinator startup accelerator. Although Loopt achieved moderate success, it marked the beginning of Altman's journey as a Silicon Valley entrepreneur.

Leading Y Combinator


In 2014, Altman became President of Y Combinator, one of the world's most successful startup accelerators. During his leadership, Y Combinator helped fund and mentor hundreds of startups, many of which became billion-dollar companies. His reputation as a visionary investor and entrepreneur grew rapidly throughout the technology industry.

Building OpenAI


Sam Altman became CEO of OpenAI in 2019, leading the organization through one of the fastest periods of innovation in artificial intelligence history.

Under his leadership, OpenAI introduced breakthrough technologies including:

  • ChatGPT
  • GPT-4 and GPT-5 language models
  • DALL·E image generation
  • Advanced AI tools for developers and enterprises

These technologies have transformed how people write, learn, create software, conduct research, and automate business operations.

AI for Everyone


Altman has consistently promoted the idea that artificial intelligence should benefit humanity while emphasizing the importance of responsible development and safety. OpenAI continues investing heavily in AI alignment, security, and research to ensure increasingly capable AI systems are deployed responsibly.

Industry Impact


Today, OpenAI is among the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, serving hundreds of millions of users and partnering with businesses across healthcare, finance, education, software development, and scientific research.

Altman is widely recognized as one of the key figures shaping the future of artificial intelligence and is frequently invited to speak with governments, policymakers, and global business leaders about AI's opportunities and challenges.

Looking Ahead


As AI becomes an increasingly important part of everyday life, Sam Altman's leadership continues to influence the direction of one of the most transformative technologies of the 21st century. His vision extends beyond today's AI assistants toward systems capable of solving complex scientific, medical, and economic challenges while expanding access to knowledge worldwide.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Says Shailene Woodley Wanted Another Man Days After His Proposal
articles.subheading: The Steelers quarterback shared his version of the former couple’s engagement and disputed how their split has been portrayed publicly
articles.summary: The Steelers quarterback shared his version of the former couple’s engagement and disputed how their split has been portrayed publicly
articles.content:
Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has shared new details about his former relationship with actress Shailene Woodley, claiming she told him she wanted to be with another man only days after accepting his marriage proposal.

Rodgers discussed the relationship during an appearance on teammate Cam Heyward’s “Not Just Football” podcast, where he revisited the couple’s engagement and the events that followed. According to Rodgers, he proposed to Woodley in December and she accepted, but the relationship quickly took a different turn.

Rodgers said Woodley later told him she wanted to be with someone else. He described the revelation as a major turning point, saying, “She told me she wanted to be with another guy.” He also suggested that the engagement was effectively over soon afterward.

The couple’s relationship became public in 2021, bringing together the NFL star and the Divergent actress. Rodgers confirmed their engagement that same year, but the pair ultimately ended their relationship in 2022 without marrying.

Rodgers also disputed how their breakup has been portrayed publicly. He said Woodley had stopped wearing her engagement ring by March and claimed the two later made attempts to reconcile before ultimately going their separate ways.

articles.title: We were riding bikes around the street at nine. Kids at present are not granted that freedom till they are eleven years old.
articles.subheading: A two-year gap between generations does not sound significant. It may be changing how children learn to manage risk, according to researchers
articles.summary: A two-year gap between generations does not sound significant. It may be changing how children learn to manage risk, according to researchers
articles.content:
According to a recent study that interviewed almost 2,000 parents, children today are not granted the same freedom until closer to 10.8, or nearly 11 years on average, whereas parents themselves were usually let to play outside alone by the age of nine. Two years may not seem like much. Nevertheless, researchers who are examining it believe otherwise. 

Why, therefore, is a two-year delay important enough to study? 
According to Helen Dodd, a professor of child psychology who oversaw the study, there is a distinct pattern in the data: "less independence for our children now than in past generations." She worries about missed practice as much as lost playtime. It is difficult to develop the ability to independently assess and manage danger by staying indoors, thus children who do not have enough unsupervised opportunities by the end of primary school may not be able to do so. 
Children now play for an average of three hours a day, with only half of that time spent outside, according to the same 2020 poll of roughly 1,919 parents. 
The issue is not that young children should just be left on their own. Rather, psychologists contend that youngsters must be gradually given the chance to make their own judgments. Children can have brief opportunities to assess circumstances, find solutions, and recognize their own boundaries by exploring a familiar neighborhood, playing with friends on the street, or strolling to a local store.
Children are growing up in a different world at the same time. The amount of freedom parents are ready to grant can be influenced by a number of factors, including busier roadways, less appropriate outside play areas, safety concerns, and the increasing prevalence of screens. Therefore, rather than expecting parents to just offer their kids more freedom, the task might be to create safer ways for kids to experience independence.

Freedom still exists. Kids only receive it two years later than it used to be, and scientists are closely monitoring the consequences of it.

articles.title: XRP Pullback Deepens as Momentum Weakens Across Key Timeframes
articles.subheading: XRP falls 2.4% to around $1.38 as bearish technical signals dominate short-term trading
articles.summary: XRP falls 2.4% to around $1.38 as bearish technical signals dominate short-term trading
articles.content:
XRP continued its pullback on Friday, with the cryptocurrency falling about 2.4% to trade near $1.38. The decline comes as momentum weakens across several timeframes, with XRP trading below its key short- and medium-term moving averages.

The token remains above its longer-term trend indicator, suggesting that the broader trend has not completely broken down. However, near-term indicators are increasingly pointing toward continued selling pressure.

Evernorth regulatory milestone adds a bullish catalyst


One of the key developments surrounding XRP is the latest regulatory progress involving Evernorth Holdings.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission declared Evernorth's Form S-4 registration effective on August 27, moving the Ripple-backed company closer to a potential Nasdaq listing and its proposed $1 billion XRP treasury.

The development could expand institutional access to XRP if the planned transaction proceeds. An upcoming shareholder vote on the merger will be an important next step.

Despite the regulatory progress, XRP's price has yet to respond with a sustained upside move. Broader market selling pressure continues to outweigh the positive news in the short term.

Technical indicators remain under pressure


XRP/USD is currently trading below the 20-hour moving average at approximately $1.3947 and the 50-hour moving average at $1.4191.

The Ichimoku Kijun level around $1.4027 is also acting as nearby resistance. A sustained move above this level could provide an early indication that selling pressure is easing.

Momentum indicators remain largely bearish. The MACD and ADX point toward continued downside pressure, while the Relative Strength Index is around 38.5, reflecting weak momentum without yet reaching deeply oversold territory.

Other indicators, including CCI and Bull/Bear Power, continue to favour sellers. Stochastic RSI, meanwhile, suggests that some short-term exhaustion may be developing.

XRP faces a key support test


Over the next two to three trading days, XRP could remain within a projected range of roughly $1.24 to $1.44.

Current technical projections give a higher probability to a downward move than an upward breakout, with downside risk estimated at 67% compared with 33% for an advance.

A recovery above the $1.4027 resistance area would strengthen the short-term bullish case. However, failure to reclaim that level could leave XRP vulnerable to another decline toward lower support levels.

Traders Union expert Anton Kharitonov said the regulatory development surrounding Evernorth is significant, but technical conditions remain cautious.

"Until we see price reclaim key averages and a clear break above $1.4027, I stay defensive and avoid premature upside bets," Kharitonov said.

What traders are watching next


The upcoming Evernorth shareholder vote could become an important catalyst for XRP, particularly if the proposed XRP treasury and Nasdaq listing move forward.

At the same time, traders will be watching whether XRP can regain its short-term moving averages or instead break below nearby support.

For now, the market remains caught between a potentially important institutional catalyst and weakening short-term momentum. A decisive break above resistance or below support could determine XRP's next major move.

articles.title: Smoke is not one of the six commonplace things that quietly damage your lungs.
articles.subheading: The majority of people are already aware that pollutants and cigarettes are harmful to the lungs. Fewer are aware that a hot tub or a pet bird may also be causing harm.
articles.summary: The majority of people are already aware that pollutants and cigarettes are harmful to the lungs. Fewer are aware that a hot tub or a pet bird may also be causing harm.
articles.content:
Every breath keeps us alive because our lungs work nonstop and without complaint. However, not everything that is harmful to them is recognizable as chemical vapours or smoke. What are these less recognized lung dangers, and what harm do they truly cause?

Birds are at the top of the list, and this is true not only for owners. The American Lung Association states that "bird fancier's lung" (officially known as hypersensitivity pneumonitis) is caused by inhaling microscopic particles present in bird droppings and feathers. Over time, frequent exposure can silently damage lung tissue if left untreated.

Aside from the apparent annoyance of having them around, cockroaches pose a risk of their own. Cockroach waste and body parts include allergens that are highly associated with asthma, according to research from the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America. This is particularly prevalent in homes and businesses where infestations go undetected.

Strangely, airbags also present a short-term but significant risk. In order to facilitate the bag's smooth unfolding, they produce a burst of fine chemical powder when they deploy. If this powder is directly breathed during a crash, it can result in short-term chemical pneumonitis.

Ironically, humidifiers are supposed to aid with breathing, but if they are neglected, they can have disastrous consequences. According to the American Lung Association, dirty humidifiers can harbour germs and fungus, which can cause "humidifier lung," a condition that is brought on by inhaling tainted mist.

he risk is the same for hot tubs. Warm water systems are conducive to the growth of bacteria such as Mycobacterium avium complex, and breathing in the fumes has been connected to a lung ailment known as "hot tub lung."

Even fireworks, as merely aesthetically pleasing as they may appear, are expensive. Their vibrant hues are caused by metal salts, such as strontium, copper, and titanium, which are discharged into the atmosphere as fine particulate matter and can exacerbate asthma and other respiratory disorders.

This has nothing to do with your pet parakeet. Because lung injury, unlike smoke, rarely has a warning smell, it requires attention to maintenance, ventilation, and exposure.

Do you use a humidifier, have birds, or a hot tub? How do you maintain air safety?

articles.title: Wingstop Launches $27.99 Wing Pass With 18 Weeks of Wings
articles.subheading: Only 100 Club Wingstop members can grab the limited pass, which promises a 20-wing watch party bundle every Sunday of the regular football season
articles.summary: Only 100 Club Wingstop members can grab the limited pass, which promises a 20-wing watch party bundle every Sunday of the regular football season
articles.content:
Wingstop is making a bold offer to football fans: pay $27.99 once and get access to up to 18 watch-party bundles throughout the regular season.

The restaurant chain announced its first-ever Wing Pass on September 9, giving just 100 Club Wingstop members the chance to claim the deal. Each weekly bundle comes with 20 classic wings, a large fry and a large ranch, with the wings available in up to four flavors.

The pass is designed around the 18-week regular football season. Passholders will receive a new Watch Party Bundle offer through their Wingstop app account every Sunday morning, ready to redeem for game day.

That makes the promotion particularly unusual because the $27.99 price is the same as the price of a single Watch Party Bundle, according to Wingstop. But the offer is extremely limited, with only 100 passes available.

The Wing Pass goes on sale September 10 at 12 p.m. Central Time exclusively through Wingstop's online shop. It is available to Club Wingstop members in the United States while supplies last.

The promotion comes as Wingstop looks to make itself part of the weekly football routine. The company launched Club Wingstop earlier this year as a loyalty program offering members perks such as exclusive flavor releases, group ordering, merchandise drops and members-only experiences.

Wingstop is also using the football-season launch to introduce its Lemon Pepper Trio. Alongside its original Lemon Pepper flavor, the chain is adding Lemon Pepper Chili Crunch and Lemon Pepper Chili Glaze. The new flavors become available to Club Wingstop members on September 10 before their nationwide limited-time launch on September 15.

The company, which is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, currently operates more than 3,000 restaurants worldwide, according to its latest announcement. It has increasingly leaned into digital ordering and loyalty programs as it expands its U.S. and international business.

For fans lucky enough to claim one of the 100 passes, the real challenge may not be deciding what to eat on game day.

It may be getting the pass before everyone else does.

articles.title: RuPaul’s Drag Race UK Leaves BBC as WOW Presents Plus Takes Over
articles.subheading: The BBC cited significant financial pressures as the hit drag competition moves to streaming, with a UK All Stars edition planned for 2027
articles.summary: The BBC cited significant financial pressures as the hit drag competition moves to streaming, with a UK All Stars edition planned for 2027
articles.content:
RuPaul’s Drag Race UK is leaving the BBC after eight seasons, but the franchise is not ending. It is moving to WOW Presents Plus, the streaming service operated by World of Wonder, the show's production company.

The BBC confirmed the move after citing “significant financial pressures” and the need to make savings. The broadcaster said it had made a difficult decision while expressing pride in the show's run and thanking RuPaul, World of Wonder and everyone involved with the program.

The current eighth season will continue airing on BBC Three and BBC iPlayer. Future seasons will move to WOW Presents Plus, which will also become the new home for RuPaul’s Drag Race UK vs. The World.

The change marks a major shift for a show that has helped bring British drag culture to a mainstream television audience. Drag Race UK launched in 2019, with RuPaul serving as host and head judge alongside Michelle Visage, Alan Carr and Graham Norton.

But fans will not have to wait long for another major chapter. RuPaul’s Drag Race UK: All Stars, the first UK edition of the All Stars format, is scheduled to premiere on WOW Presents Plus in autumn 2027. The series will bring back previous contestants for another chance at the crown.

The move comes as the BBC faces a wider financial squeeze. The corporation is pursuing £500 million in savings over two years, with spending reductions affecting its programming and wider operations.

For WOW Presents Plus, meanwhile, the move gives the platform greater control over one of the franchise's most established international editions. Its website already lists Drag Race UK among its available programming, including the show's existing seasons.

So while the BBC era is coming to an end, the UK's drag race is far from over. The next chapter will take place primarily on streaming, with All Stars set to give familiar queens another shot at the spotlight in 2027.

articles.title: David Garcia and the platform that outlived the pandemic
articles.subheading: Opinions expressed by Digital Journal contributors are their own.
articles.summary: Opinions expressed by Digital Journal contributors are their own.
articles.content:
Renewing a driver’s license in Honduras always meant standing in line. Citizens travelled to a transit office, handed over documents, waited, and had to complete face-to-face verification. When COVID-19 restrictions closed access to government buildings in 2020, that entire process had nowhere to go. The service still had legal obligations attached to it, and the people who needed it still needed it. The software architect who built the way out was David Garcia, whose online renewal platform for the National Directorate of Road Safety and Transport has since processed more than a million renewals.

“The challenge was to keep an essential public service operating while reducing physical contact and maintaining the controls required for a legally valid renewal,” Garcia said of the period. That last clause carries the weight. A license is a legal document, and a government cannot simply relax its verification standards because its offices are shut.

Garcia is careful about how the project’s origins get described. His documented role was to design and implement the digital platform for the DNVT and connect it to the government’s existing licensing infrastructure. “I would be careful about describing it as one person’s idea, because a project like this involved an institutional need and technical execution working together,” he said. “My responsibility was to turn that need into a secure, usable online process.”

The hardest requirement was identity. Proving that a citizen is who they claim to be, without that citizen ever entering a room, drove the platform’s architecture. One check would never carry that weight alone, so Garcia layered several: secure login, document submission, CAPTCHA, two-factor authentication, validation against government records, and a scheduled video interview conducted over Zoom.

“The video interview preserved an important human verification step without requiring the citizen to appear at an office,” he said. The Zoom component was subsequently examined by outside reviewers, passing Tier 2 Focused Security Testing in February 2021 and a further security re-review in 2023, independent validation for an integration handling sensitive government data.

The heaviest engineering, though, sat somewhere less visible. NACMIS, the national licensing system Garcia had helped build years earlier, remained the authoritative record. The new public-facing platform had to move in step with it. “The online platform had to synchronize identity data, application status, staff actions, documents, and notifications without creating a separate version of the truth,” he said. Security features mattered, but coordinating an entire citizen workflow around a two-decade-old core system was the larger problem.

It was built as a full operating platform, well past the scope of an emergency web form, and included automated renewal workflows and internal management tools for DNVT staff alongside the security controls. That decision explains its afterlife. The channel stayed open once restrictions lifted, and the department kept running it. Adoption, in Garcia’s framing, was the real signal. He declines to name a single moment when public trust arrived, describing it instead as something visible through sustained use.

Designing for the general public also imposed constraints that rarely trouble enterprise software. The platform had to serve citizens with widely varying levels of digital experience, from both desktop and mobile devices, many of them attempting the process for the first time. The complexity went where users could not see it. The citizen-facing steps stayed as plain as the legal requirements allowed.

Seen against the rest of his portfolio, the renewal system fits a pattern. NACMIS centralized sensitive government records. The renewal platform let citizens reach that infrastructure remotely while preserving validation and traceability. The Honduras–Spain license exchange service he later architected pushed the same idea across an international border, using secure SOAP services, digital certificates, SCSP v3 requirements, and automated legal-equivalency checks. “In each case, the goal was to reduce manual friction without weakening trust in the data,” he said.

Twenty years of this work licensing infrastructure, a Violence Observatory information system, cross-border interoperability has left Garcia, now working in British Columbia’s private sector, with a plain view of what digital government demands. He is reluctant to compare jurisdictions he has not worked inside. He is direct about the mistake he sees most often.

“Putting a paper form on a website is not enough,” he said. “A government should first identify the authoritative data, the legal controls, the points where citizens lose time, and the steps that can be safely automated.”

articles.title: South Korean Police Arrest Three in $9 Million XRP Investment Scam
articles.subheading: South Korean authorities have arrested three people accused of orchestrating a large-scale cryptocurrency investment scam that allegedly stole
articles.summary: South Korean authorities have arrested three people accused of orchestrating a large-scale cryptocurrency investment scam that allegedly stole
articles.content:
12.3 billion won (approximately $9 million) from 71 investors through a fake XRP investment platform. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announced that the suspects collected roughly 3.4 million XRP from victims over the course of a week in October before shutting down the fraudulent website and disappearing with the funds.

Fake Investment Platform Promised Guaranteed Profits


Investigators say the group operated a website called Fxrpntwork.com, falsely presenting it as a legitimate XRP investment service. The platform advertised guaranteed monthly returns of between 1.5% and 1.8% while assuring investors that their principal investments were fully protected.

To build credibility, the suspects promoted the scheme through online blogs, news-style articles, and YouTube videos, encouraging investors to transfer XRP from domestic cryptocurrency exchanges to overseas platforms before sending the assets to wallets controlled by the fraudsters.

Authorities say the platform disappeared shortly after receiving investors' cryptocurrency.

Police Trace Larger Flow of Funds


Although confirmed losses currently total 12.3 billion won, investigators have traced 27.3 billion won (around $20 million) in cryptocurrency transactions linked to wallets associated with the case.

The discovery suggests the fraud may have affected additional victims beyond the 71 already identified.

Police also revealed they successfully froze 17.3 billion won worth of virtual assets during the investigation, though approximately 10 billion won had already been moved before authorities intervened.

Suspects Face Criminal Charges


Two 29-year-old suspects have been taken into custody, while a 34-year-old alleged accomplice is expected to be referred to prosecutors.

Authorities are also pursuing a fourth suspect believed to have fled overseas. An Interpol Red Notice has been issued to assist international law enforcement in locating and arresting the individual.

Investigators continue to examine whether more people were involved in developing, promoting, or operating the fraudulent platform.

Scam Exploited Trusted XRP Branding


According to investigators, the fraudulent website copied the names and branding of Flare Network and FXRP, creating the false impression that it was connected to legitimate blockchain technology.

Cybersecurity experts say impersonation scams frequently misuse the names, logos, and identities of well-known cryptocurrency projects to convince investors that fraudulent platforms are authentic.

Authorities Warn Investors


South Korean police urged cryptocurrency investors to exercise caution when evaluating investment opportunities, particularly those promoted through social media or unofficial online channels.

Officials warned that legitimate cryptocurrency companies do not guarantee fixed returns or ask users to transfer digital assets to unfamiliar wallets through unsolicited promotions.

Financial regulators worldwide continue to identify promises of "risk-free" or guaranteed profits as one of the clearest warning signs of cryptocurrency investment fraud.

Cryptocurrency Fraud Remains a Global Challenge


The case highlights the growing sophistication of international cryptocurrency scams, where criminal networks rapidly move stolen digital assets through multiple wallets, exchanges, and overseas platforms to complicate recovery efforts.

Authorities say the investigation remains ongoing as forensic analysts trace additional wallet activity and work to identify any remaining victims or accomplices connected to the multimillion-dollar fraud.

articles.title: Howard Lutnick Walked Into Davos and Declared: “Globalization Has Failed”
articles.subheading: The U.S. commerce secretary used the World Economic Forum stage to challenge offshoring, global supply chains and Europe's climate strategy, delivering a blunt defense of the Trump administration's America First agenda.
articles.summary: The U.S. commerce secretary used the World Economic Forum stage to challenge offshoring, global supply chains and Europe's climate strategy, delivering a blunt defense of the Trump administration's America First agenda.
articles.content:
Lutnick argued that decades of offshoring—moving manufacturing and jobs to countries with cheaper labor—had weakened American industry and left workers behind.

He specifically criticized the idea of searching for the lowest-cost labor around the world and shifting production overseas, saying that approach had hollowed out parts of the United States' industrial base.

The remarks were part of a broader effort by the Trump administration to promote its America First economic agenda before an audience of business leaders, government officials and international policymakers.

Lutnick insisted that America First should not be confused with isolationism.

“America First is a different model,” he said, arguing that governments should prioritize their own workers and strengthen domestic industries while continuing to work with other countries.

He also placed sovereignty at the center of his argument.

According to Lutnick, countries should avoid becoming dependent on foreign governments for industries he considers essential to national security, including medicine, semiconductors and manufacturing.

Then came his criticism of Europe's climate and energy policies.

“Why would Europe agree to be net zero in 2030 when they don't make a battery?” Lutnick asked.

He argued that a transition toward electric technologies without sufficient domestic battery manufacturing could increase Europe's dependence on China, which dominates major parts of the global battery supply chain.

Lutnick's comments quickly became one of the most discussed moments from the Davos gathering.

However, his assessment was not accepted without pushback.

articles.summary: A major fire at a popular entertainment venue in Bangkok has left at least 27 people dead, according to Thai media reports.
articles.description: A major fire at a popular entertainment venue in Bangkok has left at least 27 people dead, according to Thai media reports.
articles.subheading: A major fire at a popular entertainment venue in Bangkok has left at least 27 people dead, according to Thai media reports.
articles.content:
The blaze broke out shortly after midnight at a bar and restaurant in Bangkok's Chatuchak District, a well-known nightlife area. Firefighters rushed to the scene after receiving emergency calls and found patrons desperately attempting to escape as flames engulfed the building.

Chaos as Fire Spreads

Witnesses reported scenes of panic as customers fled through the venue's main entrance, which was already surrounded by flames.

Unverified videos circulating online appear to show intense flames shooting from the building while people scramble to escape. In one clip, a woman falls to the ground before managing to get back up and flee the area.

Emergency crews worked quickly to evacuate survivors and treat the injured.

Death Toll Reaches 27

Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul visited the scene and told reporters that 27 people had died in the disaster, while several others were transported to hospitals for treatment.

Authorities have not yet released the identities of the victims.

The Prime Minister emphasized that the cause of the fire remains under investigation, and officials have not yet determined how the blaze started.

Fire Brought Under Control

Firefighters succeeded in bringing the fire under control within approximately 30 minutes of arriving at the scene.

However, images taken after the blaze reveal extensive destruction inside the venue:

  • Interior completely burned and blackened
  • Severe structural damage
  • Charred walls and furnishings
  • Sections of the ceiling collapsed or peeling away

Search Efforts Continue

Local media reports indicate that several people remain unaccounted for, raising concerns that the death toll could increase as rescue and recovery operations continue.

Investigators and emergency personnel remain at the scene, searching for missing individuals and examining the wreckage to determine the cause of the tragedy.

Ongoing Investigation

Authorities have launched a full investigation into the incident. Officials are expected to review:

  • Fire safety measures at the venue
  • Emergency exits and evacuation procedures
  • Electrical and structural conditions
  • Possible causes of ignition

The fire is one of the deadliest entertainment venue disasters in Thailand in recent years and has shocked residents across the country.

This is a developing story, and additional information may emerge as authorities continue their investigation.

articles.summary: A United States service member was killed and another injured in northern Iraq on Saturday during an operation to dispose of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian attack drone, according to the US military.
articles.description: A United States service member was killed and another injured in northern Iraq on Saturday during an operation to dispose of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian attack drone, according to the US military.
articles.subheading: A United States service member was killed and another injured in northern Iraq on Saturday during an operation to dispose of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian attack drone, according to the US military.
articles.content:
The incident occurred one day after an Iranian strike on a military installation in Jordan left two American soldiers dead while another service member remains unaccounted for.

In a statement, US Central Command (CENTCOM) confirmed that the fatality happened during a controlled detonation of unexploded drone munitions. The military also reported that search teams operating at the Jordan attack site had recovered unidentified human remains, with forensic examinations underway to determine their identity.

The developments come as military tensions between the United States and Iran continue to intensify, marking more than a week of sustained exchanges of strikes across the Middle East.

Escalating Military Operations

US officials said recent operations were intended to reduce Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and to target elements of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), which Washington blames for recent attacks on US forces.

Video verified by independent sources from the Jordanian military installation appeared to show multiple impacts followed by explosions during Friday's attack.

The latest fatality raises the reported US military death toll in the current conflict to 17, including an American Navy pilot previously declared missing earlier this month.

Iranian authorities have reported that US military strikes over recent weeks have resulted in at least 50 deaths and more than 500 injuries across the country. Those figures have not been independently verified.

Regional Security Concerns Grow

Military activity expanded across the region over the weekend. Iranian media reported overnight strikes near the under-construction Darkhoveyn nuclear power facility in southwestern Iran as well as on Qeshm Island.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) stated that the Darkhoveyn facility was still in its early construction phase and contained no nuclear material during its most recent inspection, while urging all parties to exercise restraint.

articles.title: British Couple Seriously Injured After Being Trapped in Deadly Spain Wildfires
articles.summary: A British couple were rescued from a ravine in Spain's Almería province after becoming trapped in the devastating wildfires that have swept across the region, according to local reports.
articles.description: A British couple were rescued from a ravine in Spain's Almería province after becoming trapped in the devastating wildfires that have swept across the region, according to local reports.
articles.subheading: A British couple were rescued from a ravine in Spain's Almería province after becoming trapped in the devastating wildfires that have swept across the region, according to local reports.
articles.content:
The couple, believed to have been hiking when the fire spread rapidly through the area on Thursday, were discovered in critical condition by Civil Guard officers conducting a search operation near the village of Bédar. Both suffered severe burns and were airlifted to hospital, where they remain in intensive care.

The wildfires have already claimed 12 lives, making them among the deadliest in Spain's recent history. Local authorities have reported that more than 6,600 hectares (16,300 acres) of land have been destroyed. While the identities of those who died have not yet been officially confirmed, reports suggest that four of the victims may have been British nationals.

Dramatic Rescue

The couple were found in the early hours of Friday after rescuers heard faint cries for help coming from a steep ravine.

"As you gain more experience, something inside you tells you, 'Look again, try one more time,'" Civil Guard Sergeant Pedro Barre told Spanish broadcaster TVE.

Following the sound, officers climbed down the hillside and located the pair. Rescue officials said both victims were semi-conscious and had burns covering approximately 40% of their bodies.

"Being able to call out in the condition they were in was a titanic effort," said rescuer Rafael Zea.

Barre added: "We'll never forget the look of surprise and emotion on their faces."

Fire Situation Improving

Emergency services have continued containment and recovery operations across the affected region. On Sunday, Andalusian regional president Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla announced that the wildfire had been contained and its perimeter secured, allowing authorities to lower the emergency alert level.

Firefighters benefited from calmer winds and increased humidity, helping them make significant progress in controlling the blaze. Approximately 600 of the nearly 1,500 evacuated residents were permitted to return to their homes.

Residents Await News of Their Homes

Despite the improving situation, many residents remain uncertain about the fate of their properties.

Dozens gathered near Bédar on Sunday, waiting for permission to re-enter restricted areas. Among them were Mike and Belinda Lithgoe from Cornwall, who own a holiday home nearby.

The couple have spent recent nights sleeping in their camper van with their dog, Rocket, while awaiting updates.

"We're waiting to see if our house is still there," said Belinda Lithgoe.

She expressed cautious optimism, explaining that the smoke appeared to be moving away from their property when they evacuated.

As emergency crews continue their work, local communities are beginning the difficult process of assessing the damage caused by one of Spain's most destructive wildfire disasters in recent years.

articles.title: China Evacuates Nearly Two Million People as Powerful Typhoon Bavi Hits Eastern Coast
articles.summary: Mass evacuations, widespread transport disruptions, and deadly landslides highlight the growing threat as Typhoon Bavi sweeps across East Asia.
articles.description: Mass evacuations, widespread transport disruptions, and deadly landslides highlight the growing threat as Typhoon Bavi sweeps across East Asia.
articles.subheading: Mass evacuations, widespread transport disruptions, and deadly landslides highlight the growing threat as Typhoon Bavi sweeps across East Asia.
articles.content:
China has evacuated nearly 1.7 million people after Typhoon Bavi made landfall on its eastern coast, becoming the second major typhoon to strike the country within a week. Authorities launched large-scale emergency operations across Zhejiang and nearby provinces, suspending schools, closing businesses, cancelling transportation services, and moving residents from vulnerable coastal and low-lying areas to safer locations before the storm arrived.


Typhoon Bavi first made landfall in the coastal city of Taizhou on Saturday evening before making a second landfall in Wenzhou around midnight. At its widest point, the storm stretched nearly 1,000 kilometres, making it one of the largest weather systems in the region. Meteorologists warned that its enormous size meant heavy rain and damaging winds would affect a vast area, even far from the storm's centre.
Reference: https://www.bbc.com/news

Before reaching mainland China, Bavi travelled across the western Pacific, battering Japan's Sakishima Islands with strong winds and heavy rain before brushing past the northern coast of Taiwan. In the Philippines, intense rainfall triggered landslides that killed at least 17 people, demonstrating the destructive impact of the storm across several countries.

Although Bavi weakened from a super typhoon to a severe tropical storm before reaching inland China, weather experts warned that the storm still contained huge amounts of moisture capable of causing widespread flooding, landslides, and flash floods. Officials urged residents to remain indoors even after the strongest winds subsided because heavy rainfall would continue to pose a serious threat.

According to Chinese state media, the centre of the storm reached Hangzhou on Sunday morning and is expected to continue moving northwest into Anhui Province before reaching the northern Yellow Sea through the Shandong Peninsula. Authorities continue to monitor the storm's movement closely as emergency teams remain on high alert.

Emergency measures were implemented across eastern China, with more than 400 flights cancelled and dozens of train services suspended. Schools remained closed, outdoor activities were halted, and rescue teams were deployed to areas most likely to experience flooding and storm damage. Officials said these precautions were necessary to minimise casualties and protect critical infrastructure.

In Wenzhou, a city of around 10 million people, hundreds of thousands of residents were evacuated before the storm's arrival. Speaking to Reuters, local resident Li Liangxing described hearing roof tiles and tree branches crashing to the ground as powerful winds swept through the city, saying that residents were frightened by the intensity of the storm.

Authorities in Beijing also ordered the evacuation of around 100,000 people from areas considered to be at risk. Across eastern China, emergency shelters were opened and disaster response teams remained on standby to assist residents affected by flooding, power outages, and other storm-related emergencies.

Typhoon Bavi originally developed into a super typhoon, striking Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands with wind speeds of up to 290 km/h (180 mph). Although the storm weakened as it crossed the Pacific, it still caused widespread disruption in Japan, where thousands of homes lost electricity and several people were injured.

Taiwan escaped a direct landfall, but authorities warned that the storm could bring up to one metre of rainfall in mountainous regions. Thousands of residents were evacuated as a precaution, while schools closed, flights were cancelled, and supermarkets experienced panic buying as people stocked up on food, drinking water, and other essential supplies.

The arrival of Typhoon Bavi comes only days after Typhoon Maysak caused widespread destruction across southern China. Maysak killed at least 39 people, devastated agricultural land, resulted in the loss of large numbers of livestock, and even triggered two rare tornadoes in Hubei Province, underscoring the increasing challenges posed by extreme weather events in the region

A truck carrying frozen chicken was driving down a highway in Egypt when a group of thieves allegedly pulled up behind it, forced open its rear doors while both vehicles were moving and began stealing its cargo.

The most unbelievable part?

The truck driver reportedly had no idea it was happening.

The incident occurred on August 25, 2026, on the Cairo–Ismailia Desert Road near Cairo, according to reports citing Egypt's Ministry of Interior. A group of six suspects allegedly targeted a refrigerated truck carrying approximately four tons of frozen poultry.

Instead of stopping the truck, the suspects reportedly drove their pickup close behind it.

Video recorded by a passing motorist showed several individuals climbing onto the vehicle and reaching the rear of the moving refrigerated truck. The suspects allegedly forced open the truck's doors and began removing crates of frozen chicken.

Reports said approximately 105 kilograms, or around 231 pounds, of frozen chicken was stolen, although estimates in some coverage placed the total closer to 300 pounds.

The footage quickly spread online—and remarkably, the viral video reportedly alerted both authorities and the transport company to the theft before a formal report about the stolen cargo had been filed.

Authorities then launched an investigation using the footage.

Police reportedly identified the six suspects and traced them to locations in Cairo and Qalyubia. According to multiple reports, the suspects had previous criminal records involving offenses including armed robbery and drug trafficking.

articles.title: US Sailors reach a Thai beach town after 250 Days at Sea and a War They Didn't Sign Up For.
articles.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln departed from San Diego with six-months’ worth of mission time in the Pacific scheduled. Instead, it crashed in Iran and its 5,000-member crew has not come into contact with land for more than eight months.
articles.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln departed from San Diego with six-months’ worth of mission time in the Pacific scheduled. Instead, it crashed in Iran and its 5,000-member crew has not come into contact with land for more than eight months.
articles.subheading: The USS Abraham Lincoln departed from San Diego with six-months’ worth of mission time in the Pacific scheduled. Instead, it crashed in Iran and its 5,000-member crew has not come into contact with land for more than eight months.
articles.content:
The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln has arrived off the coast of Thailand in Pattaya, about 250 days since it set sail without stopping a single port—finally, a respite for the ship's crew of nearly 5,000 sailors and Marines. It was supposed to be a routine 6-month assignment across the Pacific and South China Sea for the carrier, which left San Diego last November.

So, what did keep it afloat for nearly 2000 years?

In war, and not that it was used for. The ship was diverted to the Gulf in the wake of US and Israeli military actions against Iran in late February, in which Admiral Cooper says the Lincoln dropped over 1.5 million pounds of weaponry and flew over 10,000 sorties. The situation on board allegedly deteriorated to the point where there were concerns to the Congress about food shortages, broken toilets and mental stress on the crew. The Navy acknowledged the deployment was difficult, but didn't elaborate on the Pattaya stop, citing "operational security".

The city of Pattaya has a rich past of just this sort of arrival. Decades ago, the city was completely turned into one of the world's most notorious party towns by American troops who were looking for R&R during the Vietnam War. This week's docking is no different: thousands of sailors, months of unpaid wages and a city eager to make the visitors' arrival count to make up for a tourism season ravaged by the same regional war that had prevented the Lincoln from docking.

Local businesses are making it a precious economic lifeline. Authorities set up tight security while Pattaya Tourism Association (PTA) adviser Bhunanan Patanasin said the city was “excited and ready to welcome them” ahead of the carrier's arrival. The crew will now get up to four days off before the Lincoln sets off on its cruise through the Pacific again.

Four days in Pattaya is a short interval on the long journey back home, for a deployment that started as routine, and became active combat.

articles.title: She Thought It Was Water: Student Rushed to Hospital After Drinking Fabric Freshener
articles.summary: A late-night thirst turned into a frightening mistake for 20-year-old University of Warwick student Lukia Pardoe, who accidentally drank about half a bottle of fabric freshener after mistaking it for water.
articles.description: A late-night thirst turned into a frightening mistake for 20-year-old University of Warwick student Lukia Pardoe, who accidentally drank about half a bottle of fabric freshener after mistaking it for water.
articles.subheading: A late-night thirst turned into a frightening mistake for 20-year-old University of Warwick student Lukia Pardoe, who accidentally drank about half a bottle of fabric freshener after mistaking it for water.
articles.content:
Pardoe had returned home after a university night out and went to bed around 1 a.m. Several hours later, she woke up thirsty and reached for what she thought was a bottle of water. There were three bottles on her desk—two containing water and one containing fabric freshener.

She immediately noticed that something was wrong when the liquid caused a burning sensation. Still groggy, she initially blamed the feeling on the hot pizza she had eaten before bed.

Pardoe said she continued drinking before realizing the liquid tasted strange. “I just remember thinking, ‘This water tastes really bad.” 

It was not until the next morning that she saw the empty cleaning-product bottle and realized what had happened. She began to panic and was taken to Warwick Hospital, where doctors performed blood tests and an ECG and gave her charcoal tablets.

Pardoe later said a consultant struggled to contain their laughter when she explained how she had mistaken the bottle for water. Despite the unusual accident, she experienced stomach cramps, coughing and a lingering chemical taste.

Thankfully, she recovered and has since been able to laugh about the incident herself. “It is a funny story. I’m very grateful nothing worse happened,” she said.

The student said the experience also taught her a simple lesson: she will no longer leave cleaning products mixed in with bottles on her desk.

articles.title: What Supplements Do Athletes Use and Why?
articles.summary: Many athletes are using supplements, such as protein powders, electrolytes, or creatine, to aid their fitness. But what exactly are they taking and do these products really enhance the performance?
articles.description: Many athletes are using supplements, such as protein powders, electrolytes, or creatine, to aid their fitness. But what exactly are they taking and do these products really enhance the performance?
articles.subheading: Many athletes are using supplements, such as protein powders, electrolytes, or creatine, to aid their fitness. But what exactly are they taking and do these products really enhance the performance?
articles.content:
The demands that athletes put on their body are unusual. Training may include hours and hours of exercise, fatigue from repeated stress to muscles as well as fluid and energy loss. Consequently, some athletes will resort to the use of supplements to help meet their nutritional requirements, to recover or enhance a specific part of their performance.

One of the most popular is protein supplements. Protein powders are a great option for athletes who are unable to meet their protein requirements from their regular diet; protein provides the necessary amino acids for muscle development and repair. But supplements are not necessary if someone is able to get enough protein in his diet.

Another popular and extensively studied supplement is creatine. Creatine is in the body and produced by it naturally, and it is stored in the muscles, which use it to provide energy during short bursts of intense activity. Creatine has been shown to increase strength and power, and aid muscle growth when used with resistance exercise. It's especially favored by athletes who make repeated high-power movements.

During long periods of exercise, electrolytes may be important for endurance athletes. Sweat on the body expels sodium and other electrolytes and sports drinks or electrolyte products can replace them, especially when training for long periods or competing in hot weather.

Caffeine has also been used by some athletes prior to exercise. It can make you feel more alert and also decrease tiredness, and some studies show it can enhance the performance in some endurance and high-intensity exercises. How much and when it is given is important, however, because too much caffeine can lead to unwanted effects, including anxiety, sleep issues and fast heartbeat.

Not all supplements for athletes are required or scientifically sound. Ingredients may also be added which are not identified on the label or substances banned in competitive sport. As such, athletes should be especially mindful of their dietary choices.

While supplements may play a part in sports nutrition, they won't replace sufficient training, sleep, hydration and solid nutrition.

articles.title: Italian Children Face Rising Obesity Despite Mediterranean Diet Legacy
articles.summary: Italian Children Face Rising Obesity Despite Mediterranean Diet Legacy
articles.description: Italian Children Face Rising Obesity Despite Mediterranean Diet Legacy
articles.subheading: Italian Children Face Rising Obesity Despite Mediterranean Diet Legacy
articles.content:
In southern Italy, the problem is especially severe. In parts of the Campania region, more than 40% of children aged eight and nine are overweight.

Seventeen-year-old Salvatore weighs 170kg (375lb) and struggles with everyday activities, including walking and tying his shoelaces. Doctors say he must lose weight before he can safely undergo life-changing bariatric surgery.

Instead, he has been prescribed GLP-1 weight-loss injections to reduce his appetite and help him qualify for the operation.

Health experts say Italy's traditional Mediterranean diet has largely disappeared. Longevity researcher Dr. Valter Longo estimates that only 10% of Italians still follow it.

He describes today's eating habits as the "five Ps" — pizza, pasta, potatoes, protein, and pane (bread) — replacing the balanced diet once known for promoting long life.


Doctors also point to the widespread availability of ultra-processed foods, sugary snacks, and calorie-dense meals as major contributors to rising obesity.

Pediatric obesity specialist Dr. Roberto Berni Canani says many parents do not realize their children are overweight and often seek medical care only for related health problems.

One example is 10-year-old Francesca, who weighs 60kg (132lb). Although she is physically active, her diet lacks vegetables and includes frequent high-calorie foods, highlighting the importance of overall eating habits rather than exercise alone.

Experts warn that improving nutrition education for families and encouraging healthier diets will be essential to reversing Italy's growing childhood obesity epidemic.

Michigan Records Highest Number of Cases

How the Infection Spreads


Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that infects the digestive system and commonly causes prolonged diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea, fatigue and dehydration. People typically become infected after consuming food or water contaminated with human waste containing the parasite.

Fresh fruits and leafy vegetables are among the foods most frequently linked to previous outbreaks, particularly when crops are irrigated or washed with contaminated water.

articles.title: How a Fitness Tracker Alert Led One Woman to Discover Her Pregnancy Early
articles.summary: Wearable health devices are increasingly offering users insights beyond fitness, with some women reporting that their smart rings and fitness trackers detected physiological changes linked to pregnancy before conventional tests confirmed it.
articles.description: Wearable health devices are increasingly offering users insights beyond fitness, with some women reporting that their smart rings and fitness trackers detected physiological changes linked to pregnancy before conventional tests confirmed it.
articles.subheading: Wearable health devices are increasingly offering users insights beyond fitness, with some women reporting that their smart rings and fitness trackers detected physiological changes linked to pregnancy before conventional tests confirmed it.
articles.content:
Ravika, a 34-year-old solicitor, was celebrating her birthday on holiday when her wearable device suddenly reported signs of physical strain.

Although she felt perfectly healthy, the tracker showed several unusual changes, including an elevated resting heart rate, increased body temperature, reduced heart rate variability, and a lower overall readiness score.

When the measurements remained abnormal for more than a week, she searched online and found discussions from other women who believed similar changes had signaled early pregnancy. A pregnancy test later confirmed she was expecting.

Tracking Every Change


Soon after learning she was pregnant, Ravika experienced cramping and sought medical advice. Doctors recommended additional testing to determine whether the pregnancy was progressing normally.

During the waiting period, she became increasingly focused on the health data collected by her wearable device.

She said she found herself checking the app repeatedly throughout the day and even waking during the night to monitor changes in her body temperature and other biometric readings, hoping they would provide reassurance about the pregnancy.

Ultimately, the pregnancy ended in miscarriage.

Similar Experiences Shared Online


Ravika's story reflects a growing number of personal accounts appearing on online forums and social media, where users claim wearable devices detected early signs of pregnancy—and, in some cases, changes that preceded pregnancy loss.

Another user, Sofia, said her smart ring showed noticeable temperature changes during three pregnancies. She experienced two miscarriages before later giving birth to a healthy son.

She recalled that falling temperature readings before her miscarriages left her emotionally prepared for difficult news, while similar biometric changes later alerted her to a successful pregnancy during a period when she had temporarily stopped trying to conceive.

articles.title: A Principal Lost His Job for Helping a Homeless Student. Years Later, He Watched Him Graduate as His Son
articles.summary: Rob Burnside chose to help Landerius “DeDe” Hayes when the teenager had nowhere safe to live. The decision cost him his career, but he says he has no regrets.
articles.description: Rob Burnside chose to help Landerius “DeDe” Hayes when the teenager had nowhere safe to live. The decision cost him his career, but he says he has no regrets.
articles.subheading: Rob Burnside chose to help Landerius “DeDe” Hayes when the teenager had nowhere safe to live. The decision cost him his career, but he says he has no regrets.
articles.content:
For Landerius “DeDe” Hayes, graduation day was about more than receiving a diploma. In the stands was the man who had once been his principal and who had since become the father figure Hayes now calls “Pa.”

The story began when Hayes was a junior at Lakota East High School in Ohio. His home life had become unstable, and he was experiencing homelessness. At times, he said, he slept in a car with the heat running because the mobile home where his father lived could become dangerously cold.

Things became even more complicated when Hayes’ mother moved to a new address outside the school district. Because Hayes no longer had an eligible address, the district told him he had to withdraw from Lakota East.

But Principal Rob Burnside started asking questions.

Instead of simply processing the withdrawal, Burnside tried to find a way for Hayes to remain in school. When the district told him that Hayes could not continue attending, Burnside went home and discussed the situation with his wife, Angel. She offered a solution: Hayes could stay with their family.

The Burnsides already had children of their own, but they welcomed Hayes into their home with his mother's permission.

Burnside also allowed Hayes to continue attending Lakota East despite the district's position. That decision ultimately cost him his job after 31 years in education. Burnside said he was given the choice of stepping down or going through the process of being terminated, and he ultimately resigned.

Even after losing his position, Burnside did not walk away from Hayes.

He and Angel eventually became Hayes' legal guardians, giving the teenager a stable home and allowing him to continue his education. Hayes later described the transformation as going from sleeping in a cold car and struggling to eat to finally being able to simply live like a kid. (CBS News)

Hayes even told Burnside that he could return to his mother so that Burnside would not lose his career.

articles.description: KATSEYE Is Down to Four as Sophia Steps Back and Manon’s Future Remains Unclear
articles.subheading: KATSEYE Is Down to Four as Sophia Steps Back and Manon’s Future Remains Unclear
articles.content:
KATSEYE was built as a six-member group, but two of its members are now temporarily away from group activities.

On August 7, 2026, KATSEYE leader Sophia Laforteza announced that she would take a temporary break after consulting medical professionals, with her health and well-being taking priority. Her return will be reassessed in September, according to HYBE and Geffen.

Sophia said the decision was difficult because of her love for performing, but emphasized that taking care of her health was necessary. Her absence means KATSEYE is currently promoting with four members, while Manon Bannerman remains on her own hiatus.

Manon, who is of Swiss-Ghanaian descent, is one of KATSEYE's six original members. She joined the group through HYBE and Geffen's The Debut: Dream Academy and debuted with KATSEYE in 2024. In February 2026, the company announced that Manon would temporarily step away from group activities to focus on her health and well-being.

Her prolonged absence has since led to questions among fans about whether she will return. KATSEYE has continued to publicly express support for Manon, while no permanent departure from the group has been officially announced.

So what is happening behind the scenes at KATSEYE?

Adding to the speculation, an alleged former insider recently made claims about Manon's working relationship with the group. The claims have not been independently verified, and they should not be treated as established facts.

The alleged insider claimed that working with Manon had been difficult for the team and said she frequently asked for additional rest and personal time after periods of intensive work. The person also alleged that this created uncertainty for the other members about whether Manon would be present.

articles.summary: Health officials across the United States are struggling to identify the source of a large outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection that causes severe watery diarrhoea and other gastrointestinal symptoms.
articles.description: Health officials across the United States are struggling to identify the source of a large outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection that causes severe watery diarrhoea and other gastrointestinal symptoms.
articles.subheading: Health officials across the United States are struggling to identify the source of a large outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection that causes severe watery diarrhoea and other gastrointestinal symptoms.
articles.content:
The outbreak has now spread to 34 states, with nearly 7,000 confirmed cases, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). While the illness is rarely fatal, it can cause weeks of debilitating symptoms, including frequent diarrhoea, stomach cramps, nausea, fatigue, and weight loss.

Why Is It So Difficult to Trace?

Cyclospora is a microscopic parasite that typically spreads through contaminated food or water, often affecting fresh produce such as berries, lettuce, herbs, and vegetables.

Public health experts say the outbreak has proven exceptionally difficult to investigate for several reasons:

  • Symptoms usually appear one to two weeks after infection, making it hard for patients to remember exactly what they ate.
  • The parasite is extremely difficult to detect in food samples.
  • The outbreak may involve multiple contaminated food sources, rather than a single product.

Steven Manderach of the Association of Food and Drug Officials described the challenge as:

"It's not like finding a needle in a haystack. It's like finding a microscopic piece of a needle in a haystack."

Testing food for Cyclospora is also far more complex than testing for bacteria such as Salmonella or E. coli. Large quantities of produce must be washed and processed before laboratories can even begin searching for traces of the parasite.

Michigan Among the Hardest-Hit States

Michigan has recorded more than 3,300 cases, making it the state most affected by the outbreak. New York has also reported a significant number of infections.

Despite extensive investigations, officials have not yet identified a common source linking the cases. As a precaution, health authorities are advising people to:

  • Thoroughly wash fresh fruits and vegetables.
  • Be cautious with raw produce, particularly berries.
  • Cook vegetables when possible.
  • Follow food-safety guidelines when preparing meals.

Concerns Over Public Health Resources

Some experts believe the investigation has become more challenging because of reductions in federal public health programmes.

In recent years, the CDC's Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network (FoodNet) reduced monitoring of several foodborne illnesses, including Cyclospora, due to funding and staffing limitations.

FoodNet previously collected nationwide data on infections, helping investigators identify patterns and trace outbreaks more quickly.

Jodie Guest, an epidemiologist at Emory University who previously worked with FoodNet, said the loss of that surveillance capacity makes outbreak investigations more difficult.

articles.title: Barbara Cartland is the Romance Queen the World Forgot.
articles.summary: She also sold hundreds of millions of books, created a iconic image in literature and became a huge symbol of romance for the world. So why has Barbara Cartland been virtually forgotten today?
articles.description: She also sold hundreds of millions of books, created a iconic image in literature and became a huge symbol of romance for the world. So why has Barbara Cartland been virtually forgotten today?
articles.subheading: She also sold hundreds of millions of books, created a iconic image in literature and became a huge symbol of romance for the world. So why has Barbara Cartland been virtually forgotten today?
articles.content:
Barbara Cartland was one of the most well-known writers in the world for decades. Clad in pink, with so much make-up on and a romantic atmosphere in the background, she became the “Queen of Romance”. But there was an incredibly productive writer behind the eerie face, and she started her own publishing empire on cobbled street corners and corners of her heart.

Cartland was born in Birmingham in 1901, and started working as a newspaper gossip columnist before writing her first novel, Jigsaw, in 1925. She eventually published 723 books of which the majority were romantic fiction, and sold an estimated 750 million copies worldwide. When at her best, she was able to write over 20 novels each year, dictating her work to secretaries as she lay on a sofa.

The stories she wrote were consistent and predictable. Perfect, often innocent heroines were placed in difficult situations and ended up falling for strong, mysterious men, and ultimately in love and happy ending. A Hazard of Hearts was one of her books which became part of the Cartland brand, and some of her novels were adapted for television.

Cartland was more than just a romance novelist, however. She was a writer of biographies, advice books, health guides, and other non-fiction. She also had a strict control on her image; her pink dresses, Rolls Royce and glamorous looks became a part of her commercial persona.

According to investigators, the suspect had been seen walking around the golf course while taking photographs and recording videos. Authorities said his behavior suggested he was closely observing security arrangements ahead of the president's planned visit.

Federal agents working in plain clothes alerted local deputies, who approached the individual for questioning. During the encounter, officers discovered the man was also wanted by the El Segundo Police Department in connection with an unrelated robbery investigation.

A search of the suspect revealed a 16-round ammunition magazine containing hollow-point rounds. Investigators later searched his parked vehicle and recovered a loaded handgun with an additional loaded magazine.

Given the proximity of the incident to the president's visit, authorities launched a broader investigation and obtained a search warrant for the suspect's residence.

articles.title: The truth about what spicy food does to your body.
articles.summary: With the first bite of a hot chilli, you will notice your mouth burning, the excess heat will cause your forehead to sweat and your nose to run. Spicy food doesn't actually burn your flesh. It is stimulating a strong response in your nervous system.
articles.description: With the first bite of a hot chilli, you will notice your mouth burning, the excess heat will cause your forehead to sweat and your nose to run. Spicy food doesn't actually burn your flesh. It is stimulating a strong response in your nervous system.
articles.subheading: With the first bite of a hot chilli, you will notice your mouth burning, the excess heat will cause your forehead to sweat and your nose to run. Spicy food doesn't actually burn your flesh. It is stimulating a strong response in your nervous system.
articles.content:
The main substance responsible for the heat of many chillies is capsaicin. It does not create actual heat. Instead, it turns on a protein referred to as TRPV1 which is present in sensory nerve cells that typically react to extreme heat and physical touch. Activation of these receptors by capsaicin causes the brain to receive a message that is interpreted as feeling hot or burning.

This is why you may feel like you have a burning mouth despite the food not being hot. Your body reacts as though something hot and irritating has occurred. Vessels may dilate in the affected area and nerves may cause sweating, a runny nose, watery eyes and an excess of saliva. These are ways to cope with the feeling of irritation in the body.

Capsaicin also affects the digestive system. Some individuals may experience stomach discomfort, heartburn or abdominal pain after eating spicy foods, especially if they eat a lot of them. It is also stimulating to the bowels, and, in sensitive individuals, may cause diarrhoea. But "spicy" food is not a cause of stomach damage. Tolerances are different from person to person.

Another intriguing effect: capsaicin has a modulatory effect on pain. Exposure can make the nerve cells less responsive and that's one way people can become accustomed to extremely spicy foods. This mechanism has also been useful in some topical pain-relieving treatments that use capsaicin.

articles.title: Why Your Shadow Might Disappear at Noon in Sri Lanka Right Now
articles.summary: Why Your Shadow Might Disappear at Noon in Sri Lanka Right Now
articles.description: Why Your Shadow Might Disappear at Noon in Sri Lanka Right Now
articles.subheading: Why Your Shadow Might Disappear at Noon in Sri Lanka Right Now
articles.content:
Beginning on August 28, the sun moved gradually southward over Sri Lanka, crossing directly overhead at various latitudes. cities like Kokkuvil, Nallur, Kodikamam, and Nagar Kovil experienced the phenomena at roughly 12:11 noon on the first day of the event, which started in the north of Sri Lanka. As the sun started moving southward each day, the phenomenon will spread to more cities.

What is the real cause of this, then? Sometimes referred to as "Zero Shadow Day" or Lāhainā Noon, it refers to a solar zenith passage. It is caused by the sun's apparent southward relative motion, which is a component of Earth's tilt and orbit around the sun, according to the Department of Meteorology. The sun's rays strike the ground nearly perfectly vertically when it is directly overhead a certain latitude at solar noon. As a result, buildings, people, and tall objects throw little to no visible shadow for that brief period of time.

This is not exclusive to this week either. In any place between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, the phenomena occurs twice a year: once when the sun moves north and again when it moves back south, which is precisely what is happening right now. Back in April, the similar phenomenon occurred in Sri Lanka as it moved northward, passing through places like Beruwala, Udawalawe, and Dodanduwa.

articles.title: Oscar-Winning Irish Actress Brenda Fricker Dies at 81
articles.summary: Oscar-Winning Irish Actress Brenda Fricker Dies at 81
articles.description: Oscar-Winning Irish Actress Brenda Fricker Dies at 81
articles.subheading: Oscar-Winning Irish Actress Brenda Fricker Dies at 81
articles.content:
Fricker won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress in 1990 for her unforgettable portrayal of Mrs. Brown, the mother of Christy Brown, in My Left Foot. The film, based on the true story of Irish writer and artist Christy Brown, also earned Daniel Day-Lewis an Academy Award for Best Actor. Her performance was widely praised for its warmth, strength, and emotional depth.

Television audiences also knew Fricker as Nurse Megan Roach in the BBC medical drama Casualty. She appeared in the show's very first episode in 1986 and remained one of its most beloved characters for years, returning for guest appearances until 2010.

Many movie fans remember her as the kind-hearted “Pigeon Lady” in the holiday classic Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992), a role that introduced her to a new generation of viewers around the world.

Born in Dublin, Fricker began her acting career in Irish television and theatre before expanding into international productions. Her extensive film credits included So I Married an Axe Murderer, Angels in the Outfield, A Time to Kill, and Veronica Guerin.

Despite her Oscar success, Fricker later reflected that the award sometimes limited opportunities by leading to typecasting. In a 2024 interview, she joked that while an Oscar brought prestige, it did not necessarily open every door she had hoped for

Following news of her death, tributes poured in from across Ireland and the entertainment industry. Irish Deputy Prime Minister Simon Harris described her as “a national treasure,” praising her authenticity and extraordinary contribution to Irish culture. Former colleagues and friends remembered her as a fearless performer with a sharp wit, immense talent, and a generous spirit.

Fricker’s life was marked by both tremendous professional achievement and personal challenges, many of which she openly discussed in her memoir published last year. Through it all, she remained admired for her honesty, resilience, and dedication to her craft.

As audiences revisit her memorable performances, Brenda Fricker will be remembered as one of Ireland’s greatest acting talents an artist whose work touched millions and whose influence on film and television will endure for generations.

The unrest is linked to protests led by the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which opposes the reservation of 12 legislative seats for refugees who migrated from Indian-administered Kashmir decades ago.

Authorities banned JAAC under anti-terrorism laws and launched a crackdown, while the group says it is not contesting the elections but is demanding greater local representation.

Supporters argue the reserved seats prevent local residents from contesting a significant portion of the 53-member assembly. The government says the arrangement protects the political rights of displaced Kashmiris.

The violence has created a climate of fear, with many candidates avoiding public rallies and instead holding small meetings in private homes.

Political leaders from both the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the opposition Pakistan People's Party (PPP) say campaigning has been heavily restricted due to security concerns.

The explosion occurred at approximately 8:00 p.m. local time in Kudrinskaya Square, a busy area near the Russian capital's city center. The restaurant, located inside one of Moscow's iconic Stalin-era skyscrapers, was hosting a private event when the blast took place.

According to Russia's National Anti-Terrorist Committee (NAK), a woman carrying an improvised explosive device attempted to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard at the entrance. Moments later, the device detonated, killing the woman, the security guard, and a restaurant guest.

Emergency services responded quickly to the scene, while dozens of injured victims were transported to nearby hospitals. Authorities said 21 people sustained injuries, though the severity of their conditions has not yet been disclosed.

Witnesses described scenes of panic as the explosion sent debris flying across the entrance of the building. Several people were seen leaving the area covered in blood while first responders established a security perimeter around the site.

Early reports suggested the explosion had originated inside the restaurant's kitchen. However, restaurant management later clarified that the incident occurred outside the building near the entrance.

articles.content:
It's a fitting time to reflect on the remarkable path that took him from a small Ohio town to the office of the Vice President of the United States.

Born on August 2, 1984, in Middletown, Ohio, Vance grew up in a family facing financial hardship and personal struggles. His early life was far from easy, but those experiences shaped his outlook and inspired him to pursue a better future.

After graduating from high school, Vance joined the United States Marine Corps, where he served with honor. His military service gave him discipline, leadership skills, and a deeper understanding of responsibility—qualities that would guide him throughout his career.

Determined to continue his education, he attended Ohio State University before earning a law degree from Yale Law School, one of America's most respected institutions. After law school, he entered the world of business as a venture capitalist while remaining interested in the economic and social issues affecting working-class communities.

His life changed dramatically in 2016 with the publication of Hillbilly Elegy, a memoir that shared his personal story and examined the challenges faced by many families in rural America. The book became a bestseller, was translated into several languages, and was later adapted into a feature film, making Vance a nationally recognized public figure.
